narrativeReportMd:
# MessageDefinition R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MessageDefinition` keeps the same canonical identity in R6, but local breaking changes are present. The highest-impact issues are the removal of `MessageDefinition.graph` and the required `focus.code` resource-type binding changing to the R6 resource universe, which invalidates some R4-valid focus codes.

## Scope
The analysis used the R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions and related package terminology artifacts. Inherited base-resource and base-element changes are excluded and called out separately as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R4 instances that used `graph` need a replacement strategy because R6 has no local element with the same name or cardinality. Message definitions focused on R4-only resource types need business review because R6 validators will reject those codes under the required binding. R6 also adds optional canonical metadata (`versionAlgorithm[x]`, `copyrightLabel`) that cannot be round-tripped into pure R4 without extensions. Several metadata elements retain their wire shape but have sharper R6 semantics, especially `jurisdiction` and `experimental`.

## Highest-impact findings
1. `MessageDefinition.graph` was removed. Any R4 instance carrying it is structurally invalid against the R6 base resource and generated R6 models will usually drop or reject the property.
2. `MessageDefinition.focus.code` remains required but its required ValueSet changed from the R4 resource type set to the R6 resource type set. R4-only codes such as `GraphDefinition`, `TestScript`, and `SupplyRequest` no longer validate; R6-only codes such as `ActorDefinition` and `SubscriptionTopic` cannot be represented as R4-valid focus codes.

## Findings requiring human review
The semantic changes to `jurisdiction` and `experimental` require review because the JSON shape stays valid while the intended meaning changes. The resource-type binding change also needs domain mapping decisions for removed or renamed resources.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The optional R6 additions are backward compatible for R4→R6 ingestion but not for R6→R4 round trip. The `graph` removal is the least backward-compatible change because no direct replacement is exposed on `MessageDefinition`. Required binding updates follow the evolution of the FHIR resource set, but they still create real validation breaks for older definitions.

## Follow-up analysis
A complete migration plan should use official cross-version mappings for resource renames/removals and a terminology expansion of the R6 jurisdiction ValueSet from terminology.hl7.org.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MessageDefinition` has material local R4→R6 breaking changes: `graph` is removed, `focus.code` has a required binding to a changed resource-type set, and several canonical metadata semantics changed without changing wire shape. The top uncertainty is not structural—the StructureDefinitions are clear—but the best migration target for removed resource types and `graph` usage needs official cross-version guidance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should first scan R4 `MessageDefinition` instances for `graph` and for `focus.code` values that are not in the R6 `resource-types` ValueSet. R6-to-R4 converters also need extension policies for `versionAlgorithm[x]` and `copyrightLabel`. Human reviewers should revisit metadata-driven business rules that interpret `jurisdiction` as intended place of use or `experimental=true` as temporary pre-production status.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local element presence, cardinality, type, flags, constraints, and the directly packaged code lists. Confidence is medium for the full terminology impact of `jurisdiction` because the R6 binding points to an external terminology.hl7.org ValueSet not present as a core-package JSON file, and no official diff/Jira rationale was used.

findings.title: MessageDefinition.graph was removed in R6

oldState.summary: Optional repeating canonical references to GraphDefinition were allowed.

semanticText.definition: Canonical reference to a GraphDefinition. If a URL is provided, it is the canonical reference to a GraphDefinition that controls what resources are to be added to the bundle when building the document.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `MessageDefinition.graph` to list one or more canonical `GraphDefinition` resources describing additional bundle inclusion/profile rules.

newState.summary: No corresponding `MessageDefinition.graph` element exists in the R6 StructureDefinition.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 local element list has no `graph` element and no same-named replacement under `MessageDefinition`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id `MessageDefinition.graph` is present in the R4 differential and snapshot and absent from both the R6 differential and snapshot. No local R6 element has equivalent name or target profile.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct structural removal. An R4 instance containing `graph` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6 because R6 has no element at that path. Runtime risk is high for strict parsers, generated classes, JSON schema validators, and converters that reject unknown elements or silently drop them.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The data itself is definitional rather than patient-specific, but dropping `graph` can change which resources are expected in message bundles or documents, affecting interoperability behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify or redesign how MessageDefinition describes bundle graph inclusion rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `graph` as a deprecated optional element or a clearly mapped successor only for legacy MessageDefinition data.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 element points to `GraphDefinition`, and the R6 package no longer includes a `GraphDefinition` resource or a `MessageDefinition.graph` replacement. Removing the field is therefore a plausible way to avoid carrying an unsupported modeling surface into the R6 base resource. The breakage is real because old instances with `graph` fail R6 validation, but the less-breaking alternatives have material semantic and interoperability costs rather than being clean drop-in designs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `MessageDefinition.graph` at `0..*` with deprecation text, or added a mapped successor that explicitly preserved legacy graph references. That would keep R4 instances structurally valid. It is only a partial alternative because it would either preserve a base element whose target resource is absent from R6 or create a legacy compatibility surface that validators and implementers might continue to treat as active message-bundle behavior.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but keeps a reference to the removed GraphDefinition capability and may imply R6 support for obsolete bundle-construction semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `MessageDefinition.graph` as `0..*` canonical references to `GraphDefinition`.
No element with id `MessageDefinition.graph` exists in the R6 snapshot or differential.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative and includes the required R4 `status`, `date`, and `event[x]` fields. The `graph` property is the relevant R4-valid/R6-invalid difference.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageDefinition.graph` was removed from the R6 base resource. R4 authors could use this field to point to graph definitions that controlled which resources were included in a bundle and which profiles applied. R6 implementations that validate against the base StructureDefinition will treat the same property as unknown, and generated R6 models generally will not have a place to store it.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid content that includes `graph` becomes R6-invalid as a base instance. This affects R4→R6 validation and parsers that reject unknown elements. It does not create a significant R6→R4 representability issue because R6 has no corresponding field to map back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 `MessageDefinition` instances with `graph`. For each one, decide whether the referenced `GraphDefinition` information belongs in a profile, implementation guide rule, extension, or external migration note. A transform cannot be assumed lossless because R6 does not expose a direct target element.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal could have been less disruptive if R6 retained the element as deprecated or provided a mapped successor. Because neither is visible in the base StructureDefinition, old content needs explicit migration policy rather than automatic field renaming.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id, cardinality, primitive type, and binding strength are unchanged; the binding version/content changed from the R4 resource type set to the R6 resource type set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is `required`, a `focus.code` that was valid only in the R4 resource-type set becomes invalid in R6. Conversely, R6 `focus.code` values for newly added resources cannot be represented as R4-valid values. This can break validators, enum-backed generated models, switch statements over resource type names, and migration transforms.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect or unmapped focus resource types can cause a message definition to describe the wrong payload or fail conformance checks, which is an interoperability and workflow risk rather than a direct clinical data corruption issue.

justification.inferredGoal: Keep `focus.code` aligned with the resource types available in the current FHIR release.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Broaden the R6 required ValueSet to include deprecated legacy resource-type codes or define a version-spanning resource-type domain.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `focus.code` is required to identify the kind of resource that must be the message focus, so tying the required binding to the current release's resource inventory is a reasonable R6 goal. Accepting removed R4 resource codes in the R6 base would reduce migration pain, but some of those codes refer to resources removed, renamed, or otherwise outside the R6 resource set. That makes the strict R6 binding probably justified despite the validation break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could include legacy R4 resource-type codes as deprecated concepts, or use a version-independent resource-type code system with release-specific status metadata. This would preserve R4 MessageDefinition instances whose `focus.code` values are no longer in R6. It is only a partial alternative because R6 processors would still need to decide what an obsolete focus resource means, and broad acceptance could hide definitions that no longer describe a valid R6 message payload.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve more R4 instances but weaken the guarantee that an R6 focus code names an actual R6 resource type.

evidence.detail: R4 `focus.code` has a required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/resource-types|4.0.1`.
R6 `focus.code` has a required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4`.
The packaged code sets differ: 41 R4 resource codes are absent from the R6 ValueSet and 20 R6 codes are absent from the R4 resource type set.

examples.examplesMd: `TestScript` is in the R4 resource-type code system but not in the R6 `resource-types` ValueSet. `ActorDefinition` is in the R6 list but not the R4 resource-type code system.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageDefinition.focus.code` did not change shape, but its required terminology domain did. That is a hard validation issue because `required` means the primitive code must come from the specified ValueSet. Implementations that model this field as a generated enum are especially exposed: old enum values disappear and new values appear.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `focus.code` equal to an R4-only resource type can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6. An R6 instance focused on a newly introduced R6 resource type is not R4-valid. This affects both cross-version validation and code paths that dispatch by resource type.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan all `focus.code` values. Codes still present in R6 can be carried forward. Codes removed from the R6 ValueSet need resource-specific migration decisions, often involving renamed/replaced resources or retiring the message definition. R6-only codes need extensions or cannot be represented as valid R4 `focus.code` values. Test mappings for each removed or added code used by local definitions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The strict change is understandable because `focus.code` should refer to resources in the active release, but it could have been made easier to bridge by publishing an explicit cross-version ConceptMap or retaining legacy codes as deprecated in a version-independent resource-type ValueSet.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Removed-code impact depends on whether real MessageDefinition instances used the removed resource types. The package did not contain R4 MessageDefinition examples to estimate prevalence.

findings.title: R6 adds versionAlgorithm[x] and copyrightLabel with no R4 core representation

oldState.summary: R4 has neither `versionAlgorithm[x]` nor `copyrightLabel` on MessageDefinition.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can carry version strings and copyright markdown, but has no base elements for a version comparison algorithm or short copyright footer label.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `versionAlgorithm[x]` (`string` or `Coding`) and optional `copyrightLabel` (`string`).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 `versionAlgorithm[x]` Coding branch is extensibly bound to a new R6 ValueSet with the listed packaged CodeSystem codes.

semanticText.definition: `versionAlgorithm[x]` indicates the mechanism used to compare versions; `copyrightLabel` is a short string for rendered copyright ownership/period/restriction labels.

newState.narrativeMd: `versionAlgorithm[x]` is a summary choice element and `copyrightLabel` is a non-summary string element in R6.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both element ids are absent in R4 and present in the R6 differential and snapshot. They are optional additions rather than renames of existing R4 elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 instances during R4→R6 migration. They do affect R6→R4 conversion and generated code because pure R4 has no fields for these values; dropping them loses version-ordering or rendering metadata.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of version ordering metadata can affect artifact selection and publication workflows, but the data is definitional metadata rather than direct clinical content.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve canonical artifact version comparison and rendered copyright metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because the R6 elements are optional additions and do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional `versionAlgorithm[x]` and `copyrightLabel` is forward-compatible for R4-to-R6 migration: R4 instances that omit the new elements remain structurally valid in R6. The compatibility issue is only that R6 instances using the new metadata cannot be represented as pure R4 without loss or extensions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The calibration rules treat additive optional R6 content and pure R6-to-R4 down-conversion concerns as not applicable for backward-compatible alternative availability. Publishing cross-version extensions can help downgrade or round-trip R6 data, but that is migration tooling/backport strategy rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 extensions are downgrade mitigations, not backward-compatible base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional `versionAlgorithm[x]` with `string` and `Coding` types and an extensible binding to `ValueSet/version-algorithm`.
R6 adds optional `copyrightLabel` as a string.
No R4 element exists for either `versionAlgorithm[x]` or `copyrightLabel`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses placeholder extension URLs; production conversion should use official cross-version extensions if available.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces two optional metadata elements. They are safe for old R4 content moving forward, but R6 instances using them have information that R4 cannot represent as base elements. `versionAlgorithm[x]` is also a choice element, so generated code and serializers need the usual FHIR choice-type handling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid merely because R6 added optional fields. However, an R6 instance containing either field is not directly valid as R4 unless the information is dropped or converted to extensions. The risk is data loss or converter failure rather than R4→R6 validation failure.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, no action is required unless implementations want to populate the new metadata. For R6→R4, decide whether to drop the values, use extensions, or block conversion when version ordering/copyright rendering metadata must be preserved. Test both `versionAlgorithmString` and `versionAlgorithmCoding` branches.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are the least disruptive base-resource design for new capabilities. They still need cross-version extension guidance for lossless downgrade, but preserving R4 wire compatibility while adding first-class R6 metadata is reasonable.

findings.title: MessageDefinition.jurisdiction semantics shifted from intended use jurisdiction to maintaining authority jurisdiction

oldState.summary: Jurisdiction represented where the message definition was intended to be used.

semanticText.short: Intended jurisdiction for message definition (if applicable)
semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the message definition is intended to be used.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 positioned `jurisdiction` as the intended jurisdiction of use for the message definition.

newState.summary: Jurisdiction represents the authority maintaining the message definition; intended use jurisdiction should move to useContext.

semanticText.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the message definition (if applicable)
semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.
semanticText.comment: Implementations are encouraged to migrate to using the new 'jurisdiction' code in the useContext element.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 redefines `jurisdiction` around the maintaining authority and includes a deprecation-style note encouraging jurisdiction-of-use information in `useContext`.

facts.newValue: authority that maintains the resource is operating
DEPRECATION NOTE: migrate intended-use jurisdiction to useContext with usage-context-type#jurisdiction

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id is retained with the same cardinality/type/binding strength, but its definition/comment and ValueSet canonical changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON remains structurally valid, but systems that interpret `jurisdiction` for search, publication, policy, or routing may make different decisions in R6. The binding canonical also changed from an R4 core ValueSet URL to a terminology.hl7.org ValueSet URL, which can affect terminology resolution.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misinterpreting jurisdiction can affect whether a message definition is selected for a region or authority, which is a business/interoperability risk.

justification.inferredGoal: Align canonical resource metadata so `jurisdiction` identifies the responsible authority while use-context captures use jurisdictions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `jurisdiction` as intended-use jurisdiction and add a separate maintaining-authority jurisdiction element or profile guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears to be a clearer split between the jurisdiction of the maintaining authority and jurisdictions of use, with use-context carrying the latter. That is a reasonable model-level cleanup, but reusing the same `jurisdiction` path for a different meaning creates a semantic break that validation cannot detect. A less-breaking design exists, but it has enough duplication and consistency cost that the R6 choice is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have preserved the R4 meaning of `jurisdiction` and added a new optional element for maintaining-authority jurisdiction, or required authority jurisdiction through a profile while leaving base semantics unchanged. This would preserve old interpretations. It is only a partial alternative because implementers would then have multiple jurisdiction-like representations on the same canonical artifact, making search, indexing, and policy interpretation more ambiguous and likely to accumulate deprecated representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids reinterpreting old data but creates duplicate jurisdiction concepts and diverges from the R6 canonical-resource metadata pattern.

evidence.detail: R4 definition says jurisdiction is the region in which the message definition is intended to be used.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the message definition is intended to be used.

evidence.detail: R6 definition says jurisdiction is where the maintaining authority operates and recommends useContext for jurisdiction of use.
evidence.quote: The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.

examples.examplesMd: If an R4 `jurisdiction` value represented intended jurisdiction of use rather than maintaining authority, the R6-compatible representation may need a `useContext` jurisdiction entry.

findings.narrativeMd: `MessageDefinition.jurisdiction` retains the same path and type, but the R6 definition changes what the element means. This is a semantic migration risk because old data can still validate while downstream behavior changes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a hard structural validation break. R4 and R6 both allow repeated `CodeableConcept` values. The compatibility issue is semantic: an R4 value can be interpreted differently in R6, and terminology validation may resolve a different ValueSet canonical.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review each use of `jurisdiction`. If it identifies the maintaining authority, keep it. If it identifies intended use, copy or move it to `useContext` with `usage-context-type#jurisdiction`, while deciding whether to retain `jurisdiction` for backward compatibility. Test search/indexing logic that filters by jurisdiction.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Changing the meaning in place is disruptive because no wire-format signal marks old semantics. A separate new element would have avoided that ambiguity, but the R6 design appears to prefer consistency with canonical-resource metadata patterns.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact terminology expansion of `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction` was not available in the core package, so binding-content equivalence was not fully verified.

findings.title: MessageDefinition.experimental now means no version of the artifact is ever intended for genuine use

oldState.summary: Optional boolean indicating the message definition is for testing/education/evaluation/marketing and not genuine usage.

semanticText.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this message definition is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 described `experimental=true` as indicating the current message definition was not intended for genuine use.

newState.summary: Optional boolean indicating no version of the resource will ever be intended for genuine usage; absent means not experimental.

semanticText.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this message definition is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
semanticText.comment: If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes `experimental=true` a stronger cross-version assertion and clarifies the missing value as false-like.

facts.oldValue: this message definition ... is not intended to be used for genuine usage
facts.newValue: no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage
If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.
If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id is retained with the same cardinality and boolean type; only conformance/semantic text changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Instances remain structurally valid, but business rules using `experimental` to gate production use may need to distinguish temporary pre-production content from artifacts that will never be production content. R6 examples in the package still use `experimental=true`, showing the flag remains practically relevant.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly treating experimental artifacts as permanently non-production, or vice versa, can affect deployment and governance of message definitions.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify lifecycle semantics and prevent `experimental` from being used as a temporary maturity flag.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 per-artifact `experimental` meaning and add a separate lifecycle indicator for never-production artifacts if needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that some artifacts are permanently test/example content is a reasonable goal, but changing the semantics of the existing boolean means an R4 `experimental=true` value used as a temporary pre-production marker may be read differently in R6. The same goal could likely have been met by preserving the old flag and adding a more specific permanent-nonproduction indicator, so this level of semantic breakage is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could leave `experimental` with its R4 meaning and introduce a new optional element, or a more specific coded lifecycle/use indicator, for the R6 assertion that no version of the artifact will ever be for genuine use. That preserves existing instances and business rules while making the stronger assertion explicit. The tradeoff is a modest increase in lifecycle metadata surface area and some need to explain the relationship between the two fields, but that is a moderate cost compared with reinterpreting the existing boolean in place.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds another lifecycle metadata field but avoids silently reinterpreting existing boolean values.

evidence.detail: R4 definition says the message definition is for testing or similar purposes and is not intended for genuine usage.
R6 says no version of the resource will ever be intended for genuine usage, adds cross-version consistency guidance, and defines missing as not experimental.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is not invalid in R6; it is an example of a value whose governance meaning may change. Under R6, `experimental=true` implies a stronger permanent non-genuine-use assertion.

findings.narrativeMd: `experimental` keeps the same boolean representation but R6 strengthens the meaning. R4 readers could understand it as a testing or evaluation flag for the current artifact. R6 says that if it is true, no version of the resource will ever be for genuine use and that true should be stable across versions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no base validation break because cardinality and type are unchanged. The break is semantic and runtime: lifecycle filters, publication pipelines, and production deployment checks may need new rules for interpreting historical R4 `experimental=true` values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not blindly carry `experimental=true` forward if local governance used it as a temporary pre-production marker. Review whether the artifact is permanently example/test content. If it is expected to become production content, consider setting `experimental=false` in R6 with documented rationale or using other lifecycle metadata.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 clarification likely prevents misuse of the flag, but redefining an existing boolean creates ambiguity for migrated artifacts. A separate maturity or production-readiness field would have been less ambiguous but more complex.

findings.title: R6 adds/tightens warning constraints for MessageDefinition canonical URL and name

oldState.summary: R4 had warning constraint `msd-0` on `name` matching `[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}` and no local URL warning constraint.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 warned when `name` was not a code-generation-friendly identifier. Single-letter uppercase names matched the regex, and no local `url` warning rejected canonical separators.

newState.summary: R6 replaces the name warning with `cnl-0` and adds URL warning `cnl-1` prohibiting `|`, `#`, and spaces.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation
URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

newState.narrativeMd: R6 warns on one-character names, explicitly gates the name regex on presence, and warns about canonical URL characters that complicate references.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `msd-0` and `cnl-0` have the same human purpose but different keys/expressions. `cnl-1` is a new local constraint on `MessageDefinition.url`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Both constraints are warnings, not errors, so they should not make instances invalid under normal FHIR validation policy. They can still break pipelines that fail on warnings or generate code from names/URLs. One-character names such as `A` and URLs containing `|`, `#`, or spaces are the primary affected cases.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is build/governance friction and canonical reference processing rather than direct clinical or operational safety.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve canonical artifact processability for code generation and canonical references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base design is needed because the new/tightened constraints are warnings, not validity errors.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The constraints promote code-generation-friendly names and canonical URLs that avoid characters problematic for references. Because R6 expresses them as warnings, R4 instances do not become base-invalid under normal FHIR validation. The meaningful risk is operational for pipelines that elevate warnings to errors.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue under the calibration rules. R6 already chose a compatibility-preserving warning severity. Migration advice such as not failing bulk conversion on warnings is implementation guidance, not a different base specification design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Warning severity is already the compatibility-preserving design; treating warnings as fatal is an implementation policy, not a base R6 alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 root constraint `msd-0` is a warning with expression `name.matches(...)`.
R6 changes the name warning expression/key and adds a URL warning constraint.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment remains structurally valid but would receive R6 warning-level validation messages for the URL and likely the one-character name. It is shown as old-valid/new-warning rather than old-valid/new-invalid.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 tightens warning-level conformance around canonical identifiers. This is not a hard validation break, but it can surface in CI pipelines, publication tooling, or code generators that promote warnings to failures.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Under standard severity handling, R4 instances do not become R6-invalid because these constraints are warnings. Compatibility risk appears when local policy treats warnings as errors or when generated code assumes names and URLs satisfy the stronger R6 patterns.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize `url` values to avoid `|`, `#`, and spaces, and prefer names with at least two code-generation-friendly characters. Do not fail bulk migration solely on these warning constraints unless local governance explicitly requires warning-free artifacts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping the changes as warnings is a backward-compatible mitigation. Making them errors would have been substantially more disruptive. The remaining issue is operational rather than structural.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and baseDefinition remain the same. The StructureDefinition status/version changed as expected for a new FHIR release but no rename/split/merge was found.

All retained local `MessageDefinition` elements kept the same min/max cardinalities. The only cardinality-impacting local presence change is the removed `graph` element and the added optional R6 elements, which are reported as findings.

Retained local elements kept their primitive/complex/choice types. `event[x]` remains `Coding|uri`; retained canonical elements kept their canonical target profiles. New optional `versionAlgorithm[x]` and removed `graph` are covered by findings.
`base`, `replaces`, `parent`, `focus.profile`, and `allowedResponse.message` retained the same canonical target profiles where the elements remain present.
`MessageDefinition.status` remains the only local modifier element and retains the same modifier reason. No local element changed modifier status.

Retained local elements did not materially change summary behavior. R6 explicitly records `mustSupport:false`/`isModifier:false` defaults on many elements; those are not treated as local behavior changes.

`status`, `category`, `responseRequired`, and `event[x]` retained binding strengths and their packaged CodeSystem code sets showed no removed/added codes. `focus.code` and `jurisdiction` are reported separately because their binding content/canonical semantics changed.
No local slicing definitions were found on `MessageDefinition` elements in either version.
No local fixed values, patterns, or default values were found on the compared `MessageDefinition` elements.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex value limits other than reported warning constraints were found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 StructureDefinition status is active rather than draft
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata on the definition artifact, not an instance content-model change for `MessageDefinition` resources.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that filters StructureDefinitions by maturity/status may treat the R6 definition differently.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.path: MessageDefinition.date; MessageDefinition.publisher; MessageDefinition.copyright; MessageDefinition.version; MessageDefinition.description; MessageDefinition.contact; MessageDefinition.status
nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several canonical metadata definitions and comments were refreshed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The affected retained elements keep the same cardinality and type. Most changes clarify publication/stewardship guidance, copyright ownership wording, and canonical localization/version guidance.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review documentation and governance rules if they rely on the older wording, especially the `date` distinction between publication date and last significant change and the `version` warning about `#`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: responseRequired binding description changed but code set did not
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding remains required to `messageheader-response-request`; packaged CodeSystems in R4 and R6 both contain `always`, `on-error`, `never`, and `on-success` with unchanged definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: No code migration is needed for this element based on the packaged terminology comparison.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `MessageDefinition.focus.code` depends on the release-specific resource type set. A separate terminology/resource-mapping analysis should decide how each removed or added resource type maps across R4 and R6.
The R6 `jurisdiction` binding points to an external terminology.hl7.org ValueSet whose expansion/content was not available in the core package comparison.
Inherited base-artifact changes seen in snapshots, such as inherited constraint wording and base element defaults, were intentionally excluded from local findings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 MessageDefinition diff, Jira history, or work-group rationale was used, so the report can identify changes but cannot fully explain why they were made.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official specification diff/change notes and relevant HL7 Jira tickets for MessageDefinition.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used packaged CodeSystem and ValueSet compose data rather than live terminology-server expansions. This is especially relevant for external `terminology.hl7.org` jurisdiction content.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions for the R4 and R6 bound ValueSets using the appropriate package versions and THO dependencies.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The core package contained R6 MessageDefinition examples but no R4 MessageDefinition examples in the package index, so prevalence estimates for `graph` and removed `focus.code` usage are based on structural risk rather than sample frequency.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Inspect implementation guides, production artifacts, and official example history for R4 MessageDefinition usage patterns.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`), so findings may change before final publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final published R6 core package.
